title: NGC 3923
caption: The shell galaxy NGC 3923, imaged by the Dark Energy Camera on the Víctor M. Blanco 4-meter Telescope

recognition.text: Official NSF NOIRLab / Gemini press-release image. No published audience rating.

story: Symmetrical, onion-like layers surround the shell galaxy NGC 3923 in this image, which is also crowded with other galaxies. NGC 3923 lies in the direction of the constellation Hydra.

Shell galaxies are ringed by faint, curved shells of stars. Astronomers generally think such shells form when a large galaxy swallows a smaller one, pulling its stars apart and spreading them into arcs that ripple outward around the larger galaxy.

A nearby massive galaxy cluster also appears in the frame, displaying the effect known as gravitational lensing. In lensing, the huge mass of a cluster bends the light of more distant galaxies behind it, which can stretch their images into arcs or make them appear brighter. The picture was taken with the US Department of Energy's Dark Energy Camera, mounted on the NSF Víctor M. Blanco 4-meter Telescope, which is located at Cerro Tololo in Chile, a Program of NSF NOIRLab.
